/itineraryStops/8/description.source_en:
**⟦G0⟧ (⟦G0⟧)** is **Korea's first modern public beach** — opened **in 1913** during the Japanese colonial era, predating both Haeundae (1965) and Gwangalli as a designated bathing beach. 

The 800-meter crescent of fine sand sits on Busan's southwest coast in **Seo-gu**, sheltered from the open sea by a small headland and the offshore **Songdo-do (송도, 'Pine Island')** for which the beach is named. 

The beach was Busan's premier seaside resort through the colonial period and post-war decades, hosting Korea's first beach festival in the 1920s. Modern Songdo's signature attractions are: (1) the **Songdo Marine Cable Car (송도해상케이블카)**, a 1.62-km roundtrip cable car over the bay that **reopened June 2017** after a 1988 closure — operating from **East Station (East Tower) to West Station (Songdo Sky Park)** at a maximum altitude of 86 meters, with both standard and **'Crystal cabin' (glass-floor) options**; (2) the **Songdo Cloud Trails (송도구름산책로)** — a curved 365-meter skywalk that extends from the eastern beach out over the open sea, opened **2016**, replacing the older Songdo Skywalk; and (3) the **Songdo Yonggungungu Suspension Bridge** (송도용궁구름다리), a 127-meter coastal suspension bridge that connects the western end of Songdo Marine Park to Amnam Park and the bordering Seonggol Pavilion viewpoint — opened **2020**. 

The beach's **⟦G0⟧ Festival** runs **June through August** with sand sculpture competitions, night markets, and music performances. On this bus-tour the 30-min stop is intentionally a quick coastal-air reset — guests visit the **free Cloud Trails skywalk** and the cable-car station viewpoint but do not ride the cable car (which requires a separate ticket and longer time block).

/itineraryStops/8/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Beach open 24h FREE; cable-car operating hours 09:00–21:00; Cloud Trails 24h

/itineraryStops/8/visitBasics/closed.source_en: Beach year-round; cable car closed in extreme weather

/itineraryStops/8/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Easy — flat beach promenade and Cloud Trails skywalk; bridge stairs at the western end optional

/itineraryStops/8/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Beach + Cloud Trails free; **Songdo Marine Cable Car ₩17,000 adult round-trip / ₩25,000 Crystal cabin upgrade (NOT included)**

/itineraryStops/9/highlights/1.source_en: Site of **Joseon-era waegwan (Japanese trade enclave 1678–1878)** + **Ryūtōsan Shrine** + Korean War shantytown

/itineraryStops/9/highlights/2.source_en: **Busan Tower 1973** → rebranded **Busan Diamond Tower 2021** after redevelopment

/itineraryStops/9/highlights/3.source_en: **Tower top modeled after Bulguksa Dabotap baldaquin** (NT 20, Gyeongju) — Silla heritage quotation

/itineraryStops/9/highlights/4.source_en: **Statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin** (1545–1598) — Imjin War turtle-ship hero who never lost a ship

/itineraryStops/9/highlights/5.source_en: **Citizens' Bell** — 100,000 donors; struck 33× on New Year's Eve + March 1 (Independence Movement Day)

/itineraryStops/9/highlights/7.source_en: **Covered escalator from Gwangbok-ro Fashion Street** — no return escalator

/itineraryStops/9/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Tower observatory ticket (₩12,000) is **NOT included** in this tour — guests who want to ride the observatory should plan to skip the park-level photo time and queue at the tower (~25 min round-trip ascent); most cruise guests on the bus-tour prefer the park-level photo experience plus the panorama from the park plaza itself, which is already 69 m above sea level

/itineraryStops/9/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Public restrooms at the park plaza and inside Busan Diamond Tower lobby; small souvenir shop and cafe at park-level

/itineraryStops/9/whyOnRoute.source_en: Yongdusan delivers **Busan's most-recognized 360° panorama** — and the tower's architectural quotation of **Bulguksa's Dabotap pagoda** (NT 20, Gyeongju) connects this final stop conceptually to the broader Silla-and-modern-Korea narrative the day has built across UN Memorial, Gamcheon, and Songdo. The 18:30 arrival lands at twilight — the day's most photogenic Busan skyline view from the park plaza. As the day's last stop before the cruise-terminal return, Yongdusan is also the route's **weather alternative anchor**: if rain or fog cancels ⟦G0⟧ earlier, the Diamond Tower observatory can absorb the displaced time. The covered escalator from Gwangbok-ro removes the climb that would otherwise make a 30-min stop infeasible.

/itineraryStops/9/convenience/parking.source_en: No on-site coach parking — coach drops off at Gwangbok-ro Fashion Street and waits at the Daecheong-ro pickup point

/itineraryStops/9/convenience/restroom.source_en: At the park plaza and inside Busan Diamond Tower
